sections.title: Massachusetts Pharmacist Continuing Education
sections.topic: Licensure / Pharmacist continuing education under 247 CMR 4.00
sections.subtopic: The annual requirement, its practice-specific subject overlays, what may supply the hours, and how completion is proved
learning_objectives: State the cycle total, the annual minimum and the sworn statement that carries them to the Board at renewal.
Apply the three structural limits on the annual minimum: the home-study ceiling, the bar on carry-over and the daily ceiling.
Identify which practice-specific subject overlay attaches to a registrant, and whether it is measured per calendar year or per renewal cycle.
Distinguish the two routes to authorized-provider status and the two separate 30-day clocks in the provider process.
Separate the criteria the Board applies to a home-study program from those it applies to a live program.
List the five data elements a statement of credit must carry and the period for which it must be kept.
Name the three mechanisms that relieve a registrant of the requirement and the condition attached to each.
State what a random audit requires of a selected licensee, by when, and the statutory consequence of missing it.

orientation.text: Continuing education in Massachusetts is a condition precedent to renewing a personal registration rather than a formality that follows it. 247 CMR 4.03(1) draws the requirement from M.G.L. c. 112, § 24A, and 247 CMR 4.03(2) states the consequence flatly: no registrant is eligible for renewal of a personal registration without completion of the requisite number of contact hours. The architecture underneath that sentence is a two-year renewal cycle measured in calendar years. 247 CMR 4.03(3) has the registrant submit, with the renewal application, a statement signed under the penalties of perjury that a minimum of 40 contact hours has been satisfactorily completed, and 247 CMR 4.03(4) requires a minimum of 20 contact hours in each calendar year of that cycle. So the 40-hour figure is a cycle total proved by a sworn statement at renewal, while the 20-hour figure is the annual floor that has to produce it. Every count in this area is in contact hours, and 247 CMR 2.00 defines the unit: a contact hour is a minimum of 50 minutes, or the equivalent as determined by the Board, of satisfactory participation in a Board-approved program of continuing education, and ten contact hours make one continuing education unit.

Three structural limits stop a registrant from assembling those hours in any convenient way. 247 CMR 4.03(4)(b) allows no more than 15 contact hours per calendar year acquired through home study and other mediated instruction to be applied toward the 20-hour annual minimum, which leaves at least five hours a year that have to come from somewhere else; the cap limits what may be applied, not what may be taken. 247 CMR 4.03(5) forbids carrying contact hours from one calendar year into another. 247 CMR 4.03(7) forbids earning more than eight contact hours of continuing education in a calendar day, and it says nothing about delivery format, so it binds a live conference exactly as it binds home study. Read together these defeat the end-of-cycle catch-up: a registrant who earns 40 hours in one year of the cycle has still failed the other year, and no single day can be stretched to close a shortfall however long the program runs. What counts as home study is itself a defined term. 247 CMR 2.00 describes home study and other mediated instruction as continuing education activities that do not provide for direct interaction between faculty and participants, such as audio tapes, video tapes, cable television, computer assisted instruction, journal articles and monographs, and a live program as one that provides for that direct interaction, including lectures, symposia, live teleconferences and workshops. A live teleconference therefore counts as live and does not draw on the 15-hour ceiling.

247 CMR 4.03(4) then allocates subject matter inside the annual requirement it has just stated. Under 4.03(4)(a) every registrant owes at least two contact hours per calendar year in the area of pharmacy law. The remaining allocations attach to what the registrant does or to where the registrant practises. Under 4.03(4)(c) a registrant who oversees or is directly engaged in the practice of sterile compounding, or who practises in a pharmacy licensed under M.G.L. c. 112, § 39G or § 39I, must complete at least five contact hours per calendar year in sterile compounding. Under 4.03(4)(d) the figure is three contact hours per calendar year in complex non-sterile compounding for a registrant who oversees or is directly engaged in it or who practises in a § 39H pharmacy. Under 4.03(4)(e) a registrant who oversees or is engaged in the administration of vaccines must complete at least one contact hour on the topic of immunizations during the two-year renewal cycle, which is the one overlay measured over the cycle rather than the year.

The two compounding overlays behave differently from each other in one respect that the regulation's own grammar settles. Each of 247 CMR 4.03(4)(c) and (d) states its trigger disjunctively and then states its requirement once, so a registrant who both oversees sterile compounding and practises in a § 39G pharmacy has met two triggers for a single five-hour requirement and still owes five hours, not ten. But (c) and (d) are separate subject requirements in separate subsections, so a registrant who oversees sterile compounding and also oversees complex non-sterile compounding owes the five and the three together. The distinction worth carrying is between duplicate triggers for one overlay, which do not multiply it, and distinct overlays, which accumulate.

Hours count because of where they come from, and 247 CMR 4.04 governs that. A request for provider authorization, or for approval of a program from an authorized provider, must be submitted to the Board no less than 30 days in advance of the date of the proposed program's presentation. The Board may authorize the Executive Director or a designee to grant or deny those requests, and a provider whose request is denied may appeal to the full Board by written petition submitted within 30 days of the notice of denial. Those two 30-day periods run from different events and are easy to conflate. Alongside the application route, 247 CMR 4.04(5) supplies a recognition route: a person or agency who submits documentation acceptable to the Board of having received current program approval from, and being in good standing with, either the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education or the American Medical Association CME Category 1 is considered an authorized provider. The definition of a Board-approved program adds a discretionary source: the Board may, within its discretion, accept comparable continuing education hours approved by other Boards of Pharmacy.

247 CMR 4.05 sets what the program itself has to look like, and it asks different things of the two delivery formats. Under 4.05(3) a program intended for home study or other mediated instruction shall be developed by a professional group, follow a logical sequence, involve the learner by requiring an active response to materials and provide feedback, contain a test to indicate progress and to verify completion of the program, and supply a bibliography for continued study. Under 4.05(4) a live program shall involve direct interaction between the faculty and participants, and the faculty should possess the appropriate credentials related to the discipline being taught. Under 4.05(7) evaluation runs in both directions: provision shall be made for evaluating the participants' attainment of the stated learner objectives, and participants shall be given the opportunity to evaluate faculty, learning experiences, instructional methods, facilities and educational resources used for the program. Not everything in 4.05 turns on format. The application for each program states the qualifications of the faculty preparing and teaching it under 4.05(1)(j); 4.05(5) requires education methods appropriate to the program's objectives and designed on principles of adult education, with sufficient time for each activity and adequate facilities and resources; and 4.05(6) requires the faculty of any intended program to present documentation satisfactory to the Board of competence to teach its content and of knowledge of the principles of adult education.

Two further routes produce contact hours without sitting through someone else's program. Under 247 CMR 4.07 a registered pharmacist who is a Board-approved continuing education instructor receives credit for the program taught on a one-time basis annually, so teaching the same program four times in a year yields one credit rather than four. Under 247 CMR 4.08 a registered pharmacist who enrols in a postgraduate pharmacy curriculum, a postgraduate pharmacy program or a Board-approved postgraduate medical program is awarded contact hours for satisfactory completion of each course within it, but only on two conditions read together: the sponsor or co-sponsor must be a Board-authorized or ACPE-accredited provider of continuing professional education, and the course must provide instruction in pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, pharmacy practice or pharmacy law.

Completion has to be provable, and 247 CMR 4.06 says with what. A pharmacist shall maintain documentation or a statement of credit demonstrating successful completion for a period of at least two years from the date of completion, and that period runs from the date of the course rather than from the renewal that the course fed. The documentation must contain five things: the name of the authorized provider, the participant's name, the title and number of the continuing education program, the date of completion of the program, and the number of contact hours earned. A bare attendance list or a diary entry is not that document. 247 CMR 4.06(2) then requires the pharmacist to provide it to the Board upon request and in response to random audits, which is the point at which the sworn renewal statement under 247 CMR 4.03(3) is tested against something other than the registrant's own word. The audit itself comes from statute. M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24A directs the Board to audit randomly selected renewed licences by sending the selected licensees a request for documentation evidencing completion of the required contact hours, and to post the name and date of licensees included in an audit on its website. It also fixes the consequence: a licensee who is not in compliance with the contact hour requirements, or who fails to provide the requested documentation within 7 days of receiving the request, shall be fined not more than $1,000.

Relief from the requirement comes through three defined mechanisms, none of which is informal hardship. 247 CMR 4.03(8) provides that a registrant is not required to complete continuing education in the calendar year in which the registrant has graduated from an approved college or school of pharmacy. 247 CMR 4.03(6) covers the registrant who failed to complete the requisite hours, and also the registrant who is unable because of a physical disability to conform to the home-study limitation: that registrant submits to the Board a detailed statement, signed under the penalties of perjury, setting forth the extenuating circumstances with detail and specificity, and the Board then determines whether a renewal shall be granted and notifies the applicant of its determination and reasons. 247 CMR 4.02(8), applying M.G.L. c. 112, § 1B(c), keeps the registration of a registrant engaged in active service in the armed forces valid until 90 days following release from active duty, and disapplies the continuing education requirement for the biennial cycle immediately preceding December 31st of an even-numbered year where the registrant is in active service after October 1st of that year.

worked_examples.scenario: A pharmacist oversees sterile compounding in a pharmacy licensed under M.G.L. c. 112, § 39G and also administers influenza vaccine. In year one of her cycle she completed 26 contact hours, of which two were pharmacy law and six were sterile compounding, and one contact hour was on immunizations. In year two she has completed 16 contact hours, of which two were pharmacy law and none were sterile compounding. She proposes to close the gap at a single 12-hour live conference in December. What does she still owe, and does the conference plan work?
steps: Take the annual minimum first. 247 CMR 4.03(4) requires at least 20 contact hours in each calendar year, so year two is four hours short of the general minimum, and the 26 hours banked in year one cannot help because 247 CMR 4.03(5) forbids carrying hours from one calendar year into another.
Take the pharmacy law allocation. She has two contact hours of pharmacy law in year two, which satisfies 247 CMR 4.03(4)(a) for that year.

Take the sterile compounding overlay. She oversees sterile compounding and practises in a § 39G pharmacy, so 247 CMR 4.03(4)(c) requires at least five contact hours per calendar year in sterile compounding. Year two currently has none, so five of the hours she still takes have to be in that subject.
Note that meeting both of the triggers in 4.03(4)(c), overseeing the activity and practising in the licensed setting, does not double the overlay. The subsection states one requirement of five hours.

Take the immunization overlay. 247 CMR 4.03(4)(e) requires at least one contact hour on immunizations during the two-year renewal cycle, and she completed one in year one, so nothing further is owed on that overlay for this cycle.

Now test the December plan against 247 CMR 4.03(7): a registrant may not earn more than eight contact hours of continuing education in a calendar day, and that provision is silent as to delivery format, so a live conference is capped the same way home study is. Only eight of the 12 hours issued for that single day may be applied.

Check the home-study ceiling before choosing where the remaining hours come from. 247 CMR 4.03(4)(b) allows no more than 15 home-study or other mediated-instruction hours per calendar year to be applied toward the annual 20.
worked_examples.resolution: She needs at least four more contact hours in year two to reach 20, at least five of her year-two hours must be in sterile compounding, and the one-day conference can supply no more than eight of them. The error the facts invite is treating 40 hours as a single pooled cycle target that a surplus first year can cover, and treating a long live day as exempt from the eight-hour daily cap.

worked_examples.scenario: A pharmacist is selected for a random continuing education audit twenty months after the earliest course she is relying on. She produces a printout listing four course titles and dates that she typed herself, a certificate from an authorized provider that omits the program number, and a note saying she discarded the older certificates once the Board accepted her renewal statement. How does the audit come out?
steps: Start with the retention period. 247 CMR 4.06(1) requires documentation or a statement of credit to be maintained for at least two years from the date of completion, so a course completed twenty months ago is still inside the period and discarding its record does not end the duty.

Notice where the period is measured from. It runs from the date of completion of the program, not from the renewal date, so acceptance of a renewal application does not start a fresh clock or close the old one.

Test each document against the five required elements: the name of the authorized provider, the participant's name, the title and number of the continuing education program, the date of completion, and the number of contact hours earned. A self-typed list of titles and dates carries none of the provider or hour information, and the certificate missing the program number is incomplete on its face.

Apply 247 CMR 4.06(2), which requires the pharmacist to provide the documentation or statements of credit to the Board upon request and in response to random audits. The obligation is to produce the conforming record, not to describe the courses.

Mind the clock the statute adds. M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24A gives an audited licensee 7 days from receiving the Board's request to provide the documentation, and makes both a failure to provide it in that time and a shortfall in contact hours punishable by a fine of not more than $1,000.

Relate the audit back to renewal. The statement the registrant signed under the penalties of perjury at renewal under 247 CMR 4.03(3) asserts satisfactory completion of a minimum of 40 contact hours; the audit is where that assertion is checked against the underlying documents.
worked_examples.resolution: The audit fails on the documents rather than on the education, and unless documentation evidencing the hours reaches the Board within 7 days of her receiving the request, M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24A exposes her to a fine of not more than $1,000. The error the scenario invites is treating a completed renewal as retiring the recordkeeping duty, and treating any paper naming a course as a statement of credit when the regulation names five specific elements it must contain.

worked_examples.scenario: A pharmacist plans her 20 hours for the year from three sources: a home-study module from an organisation that has never applied to the Board but holds current ACPE program approval and is in good standing; a live program whose provider filed its approval request 20 days before the presentation date and was denied by the Executive Director's designee; and her own teaching, four times that year, of a single Board-approved continuing education program. What can she count?
steps: Test the home-study source under 247 CMR 4.04(5): a person or agency who submits documentation acceptable to the Board of current program approval from, and good standing with, either ACPE or the American Medical Association CME Category 1 is considered an authorized provider, so never having used the application route is not by itself disqualifying.

Check the module against 247 CMR 4.05(3), which requires a home-study or other mediated-instruction program to be developed by a professional group, follow a logical sequence, require an active response with feedback, contain a test to indicate progress and verify completion, and supply a bibliography. A module with no completion test does not meet the Board's criteria for that format.

Test the live program. 247 CMR 4.04(2) requires the request to be submitted no less than 30 days in advance of the proposed presentation, so a filing at 20 days is out of time, and the denial stands unless disturbed. The provider's route is an appeal to the full Board by written petition submitted within 30 days of the notice of denial under 247 CMR 4.04(4), a clock that runs from the denial notice and not from the presentation date.

Test her teaching under 247 CMR 4.07: a registered pharmacist who is a Board-approved continuing education instructor receives credit for the program taught on a one-time basis annually, so four presentations of the same program yield one credit that year.

Remember the format ceiling when totalling what is left. Under 247 CMR 4.03(4)(b) no more than 15 of the annual 20 may be supplied by home study and other mediated instruction, so the home-study module cannot carry the whole year even if the provider is authorized.
worked_examples.resolution: The ACPE-approved home-study provider can be an authorized provider without the 30-day application, her repeated teaching counts once for the year, and the untimely live program is not rescued by the appeal window, which belongs to the provider and runs from the denial notice. The error invited here is reading the two 30-day periods in 247 CMR 4.04 as one clock, and reading repeated teaching as repeated credit.

worked_examples.scenario: Two registrants come up short in the same cycle. One graduated from an approved college of pharmacy in May of the first calendar year of the cycle and completed no continuing education that year. The other was hospitalised for several months and completed 11 of the 20 contact hours required for the second calendar year. Both want to renew, and both propose to note the shortfall on the renewal application and move on. What does the regulation direct in each case?
steps: For the new graduate, apply 247 CMR 4.03(8): a registrant is not required to complete continuing education in the calendar year in which the registrant has graduated from an approved college or school of pharmacy. There is no shortfall to explain for that calendar year, and the relief attaches to the fact of graduation rather than to any application.

Read the boundary of that relief. It is expressed as the calendar year of graduation, so it does not reach the other calendar year of the cycle, in which the ordinary annual minimum and any applicable subject allocations are owed in full.

For the hospitalised registrant, apply 247 CMR 4.03(6): a registrant who has failed to complete the requisite number of contact hours shall submit to the Board a detailed statement, signed under the penalties of perjury, setting forth the extenuating circumstances with detail and specificity.

Identify who decides. The regulation reserves the outcome to the Board, which shall determine whether or not a renewal shall be granted and shall notify the applicant of its determination and its reasons. Noting a shortfall on the application is not that mechanism, and neither is an employer's letter.

Note the second limb of 4.03(6), which is easy to miss: the same sworn-statement route serves a registrant who is unable because of a physical disability to conform to the limitation on home-study and other mediated-instruction hours.
worked_examples.resolution: The new graduate owes nothing for the graduation year and everything for the other year; the hospitalised registrant must file a sworn extenuating-circumstances statement and await a Board determination. The error the facts invite is treating either relief as self-certification, and treating the graduation-year relief as covering the whole two-year cycle.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A registrant must complete at least ______ contact hours in each calendar year of the cycle, and the renewal statement attests to a minimum of ______ contact hours for the cycle.
retrieval_prompts.answer: 20 each calendar year under 247 CMR 4.03(4); 40 for the cycle under 247 CMR 4.03(3).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What form does the registrant's assertion of completed hours take at renewal, and under which provision?
retrieval_prompts.answer: A statement submitted with the renewal application and signed under the penalties of perjury, under 247 CMR 4.03(3).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: At least ______ contact hours per calendar year must be in the area of pharmacy law.
retrieval_prompts.answer: Two, under 247 CMR 4.03(4)(a), and every registrant owes them regardless of setting.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: No more than ______ contact hours per calendar year acquired through home study and other mediated instruction may be applied toward the ______-hour annual minimum.
retrieval_prompts.answer: 15; 20. The cap is per calendar year, not per cycle, and it limits what may be applied rather than what may be taken.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A registrant may not earn more than ______ contact hours in a calendar day, and contact hours ______ be carried over from one calendar year to another.
retrieval_prompts.answer: Eight, under 247 CMR 4.03(7), in any delivery format; may not, under 247 CMR 4.03(5).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: State the three practice-specific subject overlays and the period each is measured over.
retrieval_prompts.answer: Sterile compounding, at least 5 contact hours per calendar year; complex non-sterile compounding, at least 3 per calendar year; immunizations, at least 1 during the two-year renewal cycle.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which pharmacy licence sections trigger a compounding overlay even where the registrant does not personally perform the compounding?
retrieval_prompts.answer: M.G.L. c. 112, § 39G or § 39I for the five-hour sterile overlay, and § 39H for the three-hour complex non-sterile overlay.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A registrant oversees both sterile and complex non-sterile compounding. How many overlay hours per calendar year, and why is that different from meeting two triggers for one overlay?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Eight: 5 plus 3, because 247 CMR 4.03(4)(c) and (d) are separate subject requirements. Meeting two triggers within a single subsection, such as overseeing sterile compounding in a § 39G pharmacy, still yields the one stated figure.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Name the five elements 247 CMR 4.06(1) requires the documentation or statement of credit to contain, and state the retention period and what it runs from.
retrieval_prompts.answer: Name of the authorized provider, participant's name, title and number of the program, date of completion, and number of contact hours earned; at least two years from the date of completion, not from renewal.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A provider must submit a request for provider authorization or program approval no less than ______ days before the presentation, and may appeal a denial to the full Board by written petition within ______ days of ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: 30; 30; the notice of denial. The two periods run from different events, under 247 CMR 4.04(2) and 4.04(4).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A person or agency who documents current program approval from, and good standing with, ______ or ______ shall be considered an authorized provider.
retrieval_prompts.answer: The Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education; the American Medical Association CME Category 1, under 247 CMR 4.04(5).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A Board-approved continuing education instructor receives credit for the program taught ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: On a one-time basis annually under 247 CMR 4.07, however many times the same program is presented that year.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Postgraduate course credit under 247 CMR 4.08 requires the sponsor or co-sponsor to be ______ and the course to instruct in ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: A Board-authorized or ACPE-accredited provider of continuing professional education; pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, pharmacy practice or pharmacy law. Both conditions must hold.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A home-study program must contain ______, while a live program must involve ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: A test to indicate progress and to verify completion of the program, under 247 CMR 4.05(3); direct interaction between the faculty and participants, under 247 CMR 4.05(4).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which two evaluations does 247 CMR 4.05(7) require, and who performs each?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Provision for evaluating the participants' attainment of the stated learner objectives, and an opportunity for participants to evaluate faculty, learning experiences, instructional methods, facilities and educational resources used for the program.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A registrant who has failed to complete the requisite hours submits ______, and ______ then determines whether renewal is granted.
retrieval_prompts.answer: A detailed statement signed under the penalties of perjury setting forth the extenuating circumstances with detail and specificity, under 247 CMR 4.03(6); the Board, which also notifies the applicant of its determination and reasons.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Continuing education is not required in the calendar year in which ______, and a registrant in active armed forces service after ______ is relieved for that biennial cycle.
retrieval_prompts.answer: The registrant graduated from an approved college or school of pharmacy, under 247 CMR 4.03(8); October 1st of the even-numbered year, under 247 CMR 4.02(8), with the registration remaining valid until 90 days following release from active duty.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Selected for a random continuing education audit, how long does a licensee have to provide the documentation, and what is the maximum fine?
retrieval_prompts.answer: 7 days from receiving the Board's request; a licensee who misses it, or who is not in compliance with the contact hour requirements, shall be fined not more than $1,000 under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24A.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Does an hour of a live interactive teleconference count against the 15-hour home-study ceiling?
retrieval_prompts.answer: No. 247 CMR 2.00 defines a live program by direct interaction between faculty and participants and names live teleconferences among live programs; home study is defined by the absence of that interaction.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What is the minimum length of one contact hour?
retrieval_prompts.answer: 50 minutes, or the equivalent as determined by the Board, of satisfactory participation in a Board-approved program of continuing education.

quick_review.text: Continuing education is a condition precedent to renewal: 247 CMR 4.03(2) makes a registrant ineligible for renewal without completion of the requisite contact hours.
40 contact hours across the two-year cycle, attested by a statement signed under the penalties of perjury with the renewal application, and at least 20 in each calendar year of that cycle.

Two contact hours of pharmacy law per calendar year, no more than 15 home-study hours applied per calendar year, no carry-over between calendar years, and no more than eight contact hours earned in a calendar day.
Sterile compounding five hours per calendar year, complex non-sterile compounding three hours per calendar year, immunizations one hour per two-year cycle.
The two compounding overlays are separate subject requirements and apply together where the registrant oversees or is directly engaged in both activities.

Provider requests reach the Board no less than 30 days before the program; a denial by the Executive Director or designee is appealable to the full Board within 30 days of the notice of denial; ACPE or AMA CME Category 1 approval with good standing makes a provider authorized.

Home-study programs need a professional developer, a logical sequence, active response with feedback, a completion test and a bibliography; live programs need direct faculty-participant interaction and faculty with credentials related to the discipline; every program, in either format, needs faculty who document their competence and knowledge of adult education, education methods that meet 4.05(5), and evaluation of and by participants.

Teaching a Board-approved program earns credit once annually, and postgraduate courses earn contact hours only where the sponsor is Board-authorized or ACPE-accredited and the subject is pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, pharmacy practice or pharmacy law.

Statements of credit carry five elements and are kept at least two years from the date of completion, and are produced to the Board on request and in response to random audits; an audit request must be answered within 7 days of receipt, on pain of a fine of not more than $1,000.
Relief comes from the graduation-year provision, the sworn extenuating-circumstances statement the Board rules on, or active armed forces service after October 1st of the even-numbered year.

decision_logic.condition: You are asked whether a registrant may renew on the hours completed.
decision_logic.action: Treat completion of the requisite contact hours as a condition precedent under 247 CMR 4.03(1) and (2), then test each calendar year of the cycle separately rather than the cycle total alone.

decision_logic.condition: A year's hours are being tallied.
decision_logic.action: Check the 20-hour annual floor, then the two pharmacy law hours, then the 15-hour home-study ceiling, then the eight-hour daily ceiling, and remember that surplus hours from the other calendar year cannot be moved across.

decision_logic.condition: The facts name a compounding activity or a pharmacy licensed under M.G.L. c. 112, § 39G, § 39H or § 39I.
decision_logic.action: Add the matching subject overlay: five hours per calendar year for sterile compounding, three for complex non-sterile compounding, and note that the immunization hour is measured per cycle rather than per year.

decision_logic.condition: A registrant satisfies more than one condition inside the same overlay subsection.
decision_logic.action: Do not multiply the overlay; the subsection states one figure. Add figures only across different subsections, as where sterile and complex non-sterile compounding are both overseen.

decision_logic.condition: The question turns on whether a provider or program is acceptable.
decision_logic.action: Ask which of the two routes in 247 CMR 4.04 is in play: the advance application filed no less than 30 days before presentation, or the recognition of current ACPE or AMA CME Category 1 approval with good standing.

decision_logic.condition: A provider's request has been denied by the Executive Director or a designee.
decision_logic.action: Run the appeal clock from the notice of denial, not from the presentation date: a written petition to the full Board within 30 days.

decision_logic.condition: The program's format is described in the facts.
decision_logic.action: Apply the format's own criteria: 247 CMR 4.05(3) for home study or other mediated instruction, 247 CMR 4.05(4) for a live program, and 247 CMR 4.05(7) for evaluation in both directions in either case.

decision_logic.condition: The registrant taught the program or took an academic course rather than attending a program.
decision_logic.action: Apply 247 CMR 4.07 for one instructor credit annually, or 247 CMR 4.08 for postgraduate coursework, checking the sponsor's status and the subject area together.

decision_logic.condition: The Board asks for proof, or a random audit is described.
decision_logic.action: Look for documentation or statements of credit carrying all five elements, retained at least two years from each course's completion date, and provided within 7 days of the licensee's receiving the Board's audit request. A late production, or a shortfall in contact hours, exposes the licensee to a fine of not more than $1,000 under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24A.

decision_logic.condition: The registrant is short of the required hours.
decision_logic.action: Identify which relief mechanism the facts fit: graduation in that calendar year, a sworn extenuating-circumstances statement for the Board to determine, or active armed forces service after October 1st of the even-numbered year. If none fits, the shortfall stands.

exceptions.text: A registrant is not required to complete continuing education in the calendar year in which the registrant graduated from an approved college or school of pharmacy, under 247 CMR 4.03(8).

247 CMR 4.03(6) opens a route for the registrant who failed to complete the requisite hours and, separately, for the registrant unable because of a physical disability to conform to the home-study limitation, in both cases by a statement signed under the penalties of perjury that the Board rules on.

Active armed forces service after October 1st of an even-numbered year disapplies the continuing education requirement for the biennial cycle immediately preceding December 31st of that year, and keeps the registration valid until 90 days following release from active duty, under 247 CMR 4.02(8).

247 CMR 4.04(5) is an exception to the ordinary advance-application route: a provider documenting current ACPE or American Medical Association CME Category 1 approval and good standing is considered authorized without filing the 30-day request.
The immunization overlay is the exception to the per-calendar-year pattern of 247 CMR 4.03(4); it is measured once across the two-year renewal cycle.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: At least 20 contact hours per calendar year
timing_deadlines.consequence: A shortfall in either calendar year is not cured by a surplus in the other, because 247 CMR 4.03(5) bars carry-over.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: Submitted with the renewal application, attesting to a minimum of 40 contact hours
timing_deadlines.consequence: The statement is signed under the penalties of perjury and is what a later random audit is measured against.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: No more than 15 contact hours per calendar year
timing_deadlines.consequence: At least five of the annual 20 must come from another delivery format.

timing_deadlines.event: Contact hours earned in one calendar day
timing_deadlines.timeframe: No more than eight
timing_deadlines.consequence: Hours beyond eight from a single day's program cannot be applied, whatever the format.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: At least one contact hour during the two-year renewal cycle

timing_deadlines.timeframe: Within 7 days of receiving the request
timing_deadlines.consequence: A licensee who fails to provide the requested documentation in time, or who is not in compliance with the contact hour requirements, shall be fined not more than $1,000.

common_traps.text: Reading 40 contact hours as a single pooled cycle target. The 20-hour annual minimum and the bar on carry-over mean a surplus year cannot subsidise a deficient one.
Treating the 15-hour home-study ceiling as a cycle figure. It is per calendar year, and it caps what may be applied toward that year's 20 rather than what may be taken.
Assuming the eight-hour daily cap is about home study. 247 CMR 4.03(7) is silent as to format, so a long live conference day is capped at eight contact hours too.

Multiplying an overlay because more than one of its triggers is met. Overseeing sterile compounding in a M.G.L. c. 112, § 39G pharmacy still produces the single five-hour figure stated in 247 CMR 4.03(4)(c).
Letting a subject allocation stand in for the annual minimum. The five sterile compounding hours or the two pharmacy law hours are floors in a named subject area, not a reduced total.
Applying the immunization overlay every calendar year. 247 CMR 4.03(4)(e) measures it across the two-year renewal cycle, unlike the compounding overlays beside it.
Collapsing the two 30-day periods in 247 CMR 4.04 into one. The submission period runs backwards from the presentation date; the appeal period runs forwards from the notice of denial.
Counting each presentation of the same taught program. 247 CMR 4.07 gives instructor credit on a one-time basis annually.
Measuring the two-year retention period from the renewal date. 247 CMR 4.06(1) runs it from the date of completion of each program.
Treating a shortfall as something the registrant can note and move past. 247 CMR 4.03(6) requires a sworn detailed statement and reserves the outcome to the Board.

Applying home-study criteria to a live program or the reverse. Only the home-study format carries the completion-test and bibliography requirements; only the live format carries the direct-interaction requirement.

sections.topic: Licensure / Pharmacist licensure, renewal and status changes
sections.subtopic: Entry by examination or reciprocity under 247 CMR 3.00, application mechanics, the biennial renewal cycle and lapse ladder in 247 CMR 4.02, retired status, duplicate certificates and the 247 CMR 20.03 change-reporting duties
learning_objectives: Distinguish the examination pathway in 247 CMR 3.01 from the reciprocity pathway in 247 CMR 3.02, and state what each one requires that the other does not.

orientation.text: A Massachusetts pharmacist licence is issued by the Board of Registration in Pharmacy, and almost every question in this area resolves into asking what the Board requires or what the Board decides. There are two doors into the licence. 247 CMR 3.01 is the examination door, with one branch for graduates of an ACPE-accredited or Board-approved school and another, through FPGEC certification, for graduates of a non-approved school. 247 CMR 3.02 is the reciprocity door, and holding a licence somewhere else does not by itself open it: the applicant must prove licensure by examination in another state or jurisdiction that requires a degree of competency equal to that required in Massachusetts and that the Board recognizes for reciprocity, together with good standing in every state where the applicant holds a licence. The two doors have different entry conditions, but they converge on the same two substantive requirements: a documented pharmacy internship and a passing MPJE score. Reciprocity is not a paperwork transfer that carries an out-of-state licence across the state line intact.

On the examination pathway 247 CMR 3.01(1) and (2) state the same four-part shape twice. Both versions require the applicant to be 18 years of age or older by the scheduled date of the examination applied for, to have completed a pharmacy internship in accordance with 247 CMR 8.01(1), and to be of good moral character. What differs between them is the academic credential. A graduate of a college or school of pharmacy accredited by the ACPE or approved by the Board satisfies it with a doctor of pharmacy degree. A graduate of a non-approved college or school satisfies it instead with official Foreign Pharmacy Graduate Examination Committee certification from NABP, an official copy of the FPGEC certificate submitted to the Board, and official notification of that certification received by the Board from NABP. The substitution is credential for credential. It does nothing at all to the internship requirement, which appears in both lists in identical terms.

Eligibility only gets the applicant as far as the examinations. 247 CMR 3.01(4) and (5) require passing both NAPLEX and MPJE with a score of not less than 75% on each, and 247 CMR 3.01(6) allows re-examination on either or both on a new application to the Board or a Board-approved testing service with all required fees. The provision that actually decides examination questions is 247 CMR 3.01(7), and it is not a cap on attempts. An applicant who fails one examination must reapply to sit the failed one within one year of the administration date of the original examination for both examination scores to be considered together, and the same year also bounds the result: if the applicant does not pass both NAPLEX and MPJE within that one-year period, the applicant must apply to retake both. Reapplying in time is therefore necessary but not sufficient, because the retake has to be passed inside the year as well. Read that way, the clock is a shelf life for the score already earned, so the thing put at risk by delay is the examination the applicant had already passed.

The reciprocity door in 247 CMR 3.02 opens only if the other state or jurisdiction requires a degree of competency equal to that required of applicants in Massachusetts and the Board recognises that jurisdiction for purposes of licensure by reciprocity. The applicant files a preliminary application with NABP, and NABP, as agent of the Board, conducts the preliminary evaluation of the applicant's qualifications. Agent is the operative word. 247 CMR 3.02(1)(b) gives the Board the final determination of any applicant's eligibility, and 247 CMR 3.02(1)(a) lets an applicant whom NABP has notified that she does not meet the requirements request in writing that the Board review the basis of NABP's decision. An approved reciprocity application is valid for one year after the date of approval by NABP. The requirements themselves still include documentation of internship experience, a passing score of at least 75% on the MPJE, and personal appearance before the Board if requested; for a graduate of a non-approved school the Board must in addition receive an official copy of the applicant's FPGEC certificate from NABP.

Underneath both doors sits a set of application mechanics that decides more questions than its dullness suggests. Under 247 CMR 3.01(3) a completed application for examination must be fully and correctly completed by the applicant and must include a recent passport-size photograph showing the applicant's likeness, a certified birth certificate or other sufficient proof of place and date of birth, written notification to the Board or the Board's designee in the case of a name change, and payment of all required fees unless waived in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, § 1B. Two consequences follow, and they work together. 247 CMR 3.01(8) lets the Board refuse to consider any application that has not been properly completed, so an incomplete application is not something the Board is obliged to cure or to chase. And 247 CMR 3.01(9) makes all fees submitted in connection with a licensure application that the Board has reviewed and acted upon non-refundable, with the same non-refundability stated for reciprocity applications at 247 CMR 3.02(1)(d). Refusing to consider an application is still acting on it, which is why the fee does not come back.

Getting the licence and keeping it are separate problems, and the second one runs on a fixed calendar rather than on the licensee's own anniversary. Under 247 CMR 4.02(1) all personal registrations expire on December 31st of each even-numbered year and shall be renewed prior to January 1st of the following year if the registrant intends to continue practising pharmacy. 247 CMR 4.02(2) lets a registrant who did not renew before the expiration date renew on payment of an annual licence fee, applicable back licence fees and a late fee, and 247 CMR 4.02(3) states the price of practising in the meantime: any practice of pharmacy after the expiration of the personal registration constitutes the unlicensed practice of pharmacy and is subject to the penalties established for it. Paying is a step in renewing, not a renewal. The ladder then lengthens with the lapse. Failure to renew for more than 60 days, where the registration was not suspended or revoked, means renewal on satisfying conditions imposed by the Board, which may include the completion of additional contact hours of continuing education. Failure to renew for more than two years, again where the registration was not suspended or revoked, means taking and passing the MPJE and meeting all other conditions determined by the Board.

Three boundaries around that ladder are worth fixing early, because each is a place where a neighbouring rule is easy to import by accident or a real one easy to miss. The first is the qualifier that 247 CMR 4.02(4) and (5) each carry in their own text: they govern an applicant whose personal registration has not been suspended or revoked by the Board. A registration that was suspended or revoked travels a different route back, and that route is not taught in this section. The second is that 247 CMR 4.02 is only the renewal and lapse half of 247 CMR 4.00. Continuing education appears here only as something the Board may require more of after a lapse of more than 60 days; the continuing education requirement itself, with its own hour structure, programme approval and recordkeeping, is a separate subject and is deliberately outside the scope declared for this section. The third is 247 CMR 4.02(8): under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 1B(c), the personal registration of a registrant engaged in active service in the armed forces remains valid until 90 days following the registrant's release from active duty, so the December 31st expiration and the ladder behind it do not run against a registrant while she serves.

Three smaller regimes finish the picture, and in each of them the intuitive answer is the wrong one. 247 CMR 3.04 lets a licensee whose licence is not surrendered, suspended or revoked petition the Board to place it on retired status, on demonstrating an intent to retire permanently from active practice in the Commonwealth and in all other jurisdictions. Retired status is expressly nondisciplinary, and it is expressly not a shelter: a licensee with retired status may not practise, the Board may decline to review any petition for reinstatement or return to current status, and nothing in 247 CMR 3.04 prevents the Board from initiating, pursuing or taking a disciplinary action against a retired licensee. 247 CMR 3.03 governs the duplicate certificate of licensure, the wallet card, which is requested on a Board-approved form with the required documentation; when the original resurfaces it is the duplicate, not the original, that shall be promptly returned to the Board. And 247 CMR 3.05 sets a floor under the whole area: no person shall be denied initial licensure or denied renewal due to any complaint, criminal charge, conviction, judgment, discipline or other sanction due to providing or assisting in providing, or dispensing medication for, reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services as defined at M.G.L. c. 12, § 11I½, so long as the services provided would have been lawful in Massachusetts and are consistent with standards for good professional practice in Massachusetts. A parallel provision for pharmacy support personnel appears at 247 CMR 8.08.

247 CMR 20.03 is worth reading closely, because its individual duties all share one period and differ only in their trigger. A licensee must maintain personal demographic information, including mailing address, phone number and email address, in the licensee's Massachusetts Department of Public Health on-line licensing profile, and must update that profile within 14 calendar days of a change to any of the three. On a change of name the licensee submits, within 14 calendar days, a sworn statement indicating that the licensee has changed name, together with a photocopy of a valid picture identification card and any other documentation the Board may require. Every individual licensed by the Board reports any arrest, pending criminal charge, or conviction within 14 calendar days, so the duty attaches at the arrest and does not wait for an adjudication. And each pharmacy and individual licensed by the Board reports any disciplinary action, as defined in 247 CMR 2.00, or loss of certification, within the same 14 calendar days. None of this waits for the next renewal, and an employer's personnel system is not the Board's record.
